results.title: 'In the Clear Moonlit Dusk' brings Japanese romance to Korean theaters
results.content: Fresh off its sold-out screening at the 31st Busan International Film Festival last month, the Japanese youth romance movie "In the Clear Moonlit Dusk" is building high expectations ahead of its Korean release on Nov 18. Based on Mika Yamamori’s hit comic series that has sold over 8.2 million copies, the movie version directed by Kentaro Takemura arrived following its Oct 23 debut in Japan. “In the Clear Moonlit Dusk” previously proved its massive appeal when all 4,000 seats in the Busan festival open cinema section sold out quickly, and when outdoor theater crowds cheered during key scenes featuring lead actor Shunsuke Michieda. In Busan, the festival screening created an electric atmosphere as fans filled the outdoor venue and cheered loudly whenever Michieda, a member of the popular Japanese idol group Naniwa Danshi, appeared on screen. results.title: JCS chief inspects aerial defense posture aboard KF-21 fighter jet
results.content: Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) Chairman Gen. Jin Yong-sung on Wednesday visited an Air Force unit and inspected the aerial defense posture while aboard the indigenous KF-21 fighter jet. Jin visited the 16th Fighter Wing in Yecheon County, some 160 kilometers southeast of Seoul, to inspect the defense posture and commanded a formation flight involving the KF-21 and FA-50 fighter jets, according to the JCS. During a meeting with pilots, Jin urged airmen to maintain a posture and capability to deter the enemy through "overwhelming" air superiority and to immediately respond to contingencies. The JCS chief also visited an Air Force unit tasked with reconnaissance of ballistic missile launches and inspected the operational readiness of the Korea Air and Missile Defense (KAMD) system, calling it a "core asset" of the country's three-axis deterrence system. results.title: S. Korea pledges $20 mil. to ADB fund for AI projects
results.content: South Korea has pledged to contribute $20 million to an Asian Development Bank (ADB) trust fund aimed at supporting artificial intelligence (AI) development projects, the finance ministry said Wednesday. The Ministry of Finance and Economy held an annual consultation meeting with the ADB in Seoul, during which the two sides signed a contribution agreement for the Korea AI for Development Trust Fund. The fund is aimed at supporting the operation of the Center for AI Innovation and Development, which will be established in South Korea under an agreement reached with the ADB in May. During the meeting, Moon Ji-sung, deputy minister for international economic affairs, also briefed the ADB on the country's official development assistance policies and directions. results.title: Cheonghae Unit to take local tactical orders in int'l operations
results.content: Korea’s anti-piracy Cheonghae Unit would take tactical orders from an on-site commander rather than Seoul’s military leadership when it joins international maritime security operations near the Strait of Hormuz, according to a motion on its deployment disclosed Wednesday. The provision came to light a day after the Cabinet approved the motion and submitted it to the National Assembly to expand the unit’s operational area from the Gulf of Aden to waters south of Oman. The planned expansion comes amid U.S. pressure on allies to help secure the Strait of Hormuz, a focal point of the months-long war with Iran. Tehran has warned that Korea could be portrayed as an accomplice in U.S. military aggression, despite Seoul’s assurances that the mission would remain outside the conflict. results.title: Salt farm owner gets prison term for abusing employees with disabilities
results.content: A salt farm owner was sentenced to four years and six months in prison on Wednesday for abusing and exploiting employees with disabilities. The Gwangju District Court convicted the 61-year-old, whose identity was withheld, of quasi-fraud and aggravated confinement. It also banned him from working at organizations serving people with disabilities for five years. He is accused of withholding about 300 million won ($225,000) in wages from three employees who worked an average of 17 hours a day for five years at his salt farm in Yeonggwang, 325 kilometers south of Seoul, until June this year. The victims, all men in their 50s and 60s, have conditions such as borderline intellectual functioning or visual impairment. They were reportedly subjected to frequent physical abuse but remained dependent on the owner due to their limited ability to defend themselves. The court also sentenced two salt

results.title: Finance minister calls for close monitoring of US midterms impact
results.content: Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il on Wednesday called for South Korea's financial attaches in overseas missions to closely monitor the impact of the U.S. midterm elections on the global economy, including how individual countries are responding. Lee made the remarks during his first meeting with financial attaches at 18 overseas missions since taking office in September, held virtually to review the latest economic trends in major countries, according to the Ministry of Finance and Economy. During the meeting, Lee stressed that South Korea faces external uncertainties, including fiscal instability in Europe and global geopolitical tensions, despite the country's robust exports. "In order to turn recent achievements into sustainable growth, we need to preemptively identify changes in the external environment and take steps to address risks in advance," Lee said during the meeting. results.title: Presidential office discusses rights protection for Korean adoptees overseas
results.content: The presidential office held a meeting Wednesday to discuss measures to protect the rights of Koreans adopted overseas and address complaints raised by them. Second Deputy National Security Adviser Lim Woong-soon presided over the gathering of the presidential task force on overseas Koreans, which focused on pan-government efforts to protect the rights of Korean adoptees, the presidential office said. The meeting also discussed government measures to resolve complaints from Korean adoptees, as well as progress in implementing recommendations by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, the presidential office said. Responding to complaints from hundreds of Korean adoptees from around the world, the state commission in March last year officially recognized dozens of them as victims of human rights violations in the adoption process. results.title: Ex-PPP leader calls for nullification of expulsion over alleged irregularities in disciplinary process
results.content: SEOUL — Independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon, a former leader of the main opposition People Power Party (PPP), called Wednesday for the party to overturn his expulsion after a member of its ethics committee alleged that disciplinary actions against him and another lawmaker had been manipulated. Hwang Kyung-sung, a member of the PPP's ethics committee, earlier claimed that the party's leader, Jang Dong-hyeok, had sought to replace committee members to cover up the alleged manipulation. Hwang's claim came after Rep. Jang recently informed the committee of his plan to replace members. Five of the six ethics committee members, including its chair, have reportedly expressed their intention to resign. Han called for the disciplinary actions to be nullified and urged Jang to issue a public apology during a press conference at the National Assembly. He was expelled from the PPP in January over all

results.title: Man indicted for Incheon commercial complex stabbing spree
results.content: Prosecutors said Wednesday they have indicted a man on charges of attempting to murder 10 people in a stabbing spree at a shopping complex last month. Choi Choong-rak, 59, faces attempted murder and weapons possession charges for allegedly stabbing the victims at the site in Incheon, just west of Seoul, on Oct. 13, leaving seven people injured, according to the prosecution. Choi allegedly brandished knives taped to both his hands during the incident before police apprehended him. He remains in custody after a court issued a warrant for his formal arrest. During police questioning, Choi said he carried out the attack out of anger over medical treatment he received at a local hospital. Choi has 10 prior convictions, including two for attempted murder, and was wearing an electronic ankle monitor at the time of the rampage.

results.title: FTC to fine 15 firms $1.2 bil. for rigging gov't bond bids
results.content: Korea's fair trade watchdog said Wednesday it has decided to impose 1.62 trillion won ($1.2 billion) in fines on 15 financial companies for colluding in government bond auctions for more than three years. The Fair Trade Commission (FTC) said the firms, all primary dealers comprising 10 brokerage houses and five banks, exchanged information on bidding yields and volumes through phone calls and messaging apps regarding 150 auctions between January 2020 and June 2023. It marked the largest fine ever imposed by the FTC in a single case, surpassing the previous record of 1.03 trillion won levied on Qualcomm for unfair practices in 2016. In 145 of those auctions, the companies went beyond exchanging information to reach agreements on specific bidding yields or volumes, constituting bid rigging, the watchdog said. results.title: Man arrested on suspicion of killing teenage victim of son's alleged sex crime
results.content: Police on Wednesday apprehended a man on suspicion of murdering a teenager who was a victim of an alleged sexual crime committed by his son. The man in his 50s was placed under emergency arrest at around 1:40 a.m. after police found the female victim dead at a house in northeastern Seoul following a report from a third person. The location was identified as an Airbnb. The teenager was found to have been a victim of a sexual crime in January, allegedly committed by the murder suspect's son. Her parents had filed a complaint in March against the son, who is currently in detention for another crime. Police plan to seek a warrant for the murder suspect's formal arrest after investigating his motive. It was not immediately clear whether the suspect carried out the crime in retaliation for the complaint against his son. Investigators said they were unable to immediately question the suspect as

results.title: Kim Soo-hyun testifies in trial of YouTuber accused of spreading false allegations
results.content: Actor Kim Soo-hyun appeared in court Wednesday as a witness in the trial of Kim Se-ui, head of the YouTube channel Garo Sero Research Institute, who was indicted while in custody on charges of spreading false information about the actor's private life. The Seoul Central District Court's Criminal Division 26, presided over by Judge Lee Hyun-kyung, held the first hearing in Kim Se-ui's trial on Wednesday. He faces charges including defamation under the Information and Communications Network Act and violations of laws against sexual violence and stalking. Kim Soo-hyun arrived at the courthouse at around 1:40 p.m. to testify. However, he entered the courtroom through a separate passage rather than the main entrance, where reporters were waiting. results.title: When fake feels real: 'Rohtko' brings one of art's big questions to Seoul
results.content: A painting does not change when it is exposed as a fake. Its price and the way people see it do. That gap between an object and the value attached to it drives “Rohtko,” Polish director Lukasz Twarkowski’s multimedia theater production, which makes its Korean premiere Friday at LG Arts Center Seoul. Inspired by a multimillion-dollar forgery scandal, the production arrives here four years after its world premiere, with its questions about originals and copies taking on fresh urgency amid the increase of artificial intelligence (AI). Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Twarkowski explored multiple perspectives on authenticity, inviting audiences to draw their own conclusions. “I truly believe that we have this possibility in theater to communicate contradictions,” he said, describing art as a way to explore complexity without declaring one single interpretation to be true. results.title: Gov't seeks to relocate Army academy out of Seoul, retain Air Force, Navy schools
results.content: The government is looking to relocate the Army academy out of Seoul while keeping the Navy and Air Force academies in place, sources said Wednesday, backtracking from its original plan to merge them into a unified military college. The defense ministry recently briefed lawmakers on the plan to move the Korea Military Academy to the central-western region of Chungcheong, while retaining the Naval Academy in the southern coastal county of Jinhae and the Air Force Academy in the central provincial city of Cheongju, sources familiar with the matter said. The latest proposal still calls for establishing a joint academy in the Jaundae military complex in the central city of Daejeon, about 140 kilometers south of Seoul, but likely at a smaller scale. results.title: [PHOTOS] Comrades honor fallen heroes in Busan
results.content: Canadian veteran Vincent Courtenay lays a chrysanthemum during the 20th Turn Toward Busan memorial ceremony at the United Nations Memorial Cemetery in Busan, Wednesday. Courtenay first proposed the simultaneous one-minute silent tribute toward the cemetery in 2007, which has since grown into an annual global event honoring those who fought in the 1950-53 Korean War. results.title: North Korea posts revised constitution online on propaganda website
results.content: North Korea has reposted its full constitution on a state propaganda website, more than 2 1/2 years after taking the document offline following leader Kim Jong-un's declaration of a two hostile state policy. The version posted on Naenara appears to be the text revised in March, which the outlet said was amended at the first session of the 15th Supreme People's Assembly on March 23. Previously, Naenara had pulled down the full text of the constitution in March 2024, along with its sections on modern history and overseas Koreans, which were believed to contain references to "unification" and "one nation." The removal followed Kim's declaration at a party plenary meeting in late 2023 that the two Koreas are separate, hostile states, and his order in January the following year to strip expressions such as "peaceful unification" and "national unity" from the constitution. results.title: Conflicting brokerage forecasts deepen investor confusion
results.content: Lim, a 44-year-old resident of Guri, Gyeonggi Province, began investing actively in Korean stocks last year, regularly reading brokerage research reports to help guide her investment decisions. But as brokerages have increasingly issued conflicting market forecasts and frequently revised their price targets, she has grown uncertain about which reports to trust. "These days, brokerages' forecasts vary so widely and price targets change so frequently that I don't know which ones to believe," Lim said. "Now, I sometimes turn to people around me or ask artificial intelligence (AI) tools for advice instead." Lim is among a growing number of retail investors struggling to make sense of brokerage research as domestic and foreign securities firms repeatedly revise their market outlooks and stock price targets amid sharp swings in the benchmark KOSPI. results.title: AI smart glasses test Korea's ability to prevent CSAT cheating
results.content: With Korea’s College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) about a week away, education authorities are training staff to identify artificial intelligence (AI)-powered smart glasses amid concerns that the devices could enable cheating and prove difficult to distinguish from ordinary eyewear. The Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education (SMOE) said Wednesday it will train 239 personnel assigned to spot smart glasses at the city’s exam sites. They will be deployed across the city’s 228 exam sites for the Nov. 19 test. Radio-frequency detectors will not be supplied for this year’s exam, leaving supervisors and trained personnel to rely largely on physical inspection. The Ministry of Education said it is considering using such equipment next year after assessing the suitability of devices currently under development. results.title: AI uncertainties after US midterms 'golden opportunity' for Korea: 2nd vice science minister
results.content: Fresh uncertainties surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) investments following the US midterms could provide a "golden opportunity" for Korea, a high-level science ministry official said Wednesday. Second Vice Science Minister Ryu Je-myung made the remarks at a congratulatory address during an AI conference hosted by the ministry in Seoul as he mentioned growing concerns in the United States that the incoming Democratic Congress could tighten regulations on AI and data centers. "There are observations that market uncertainty could increase amid potential changes in the investment environment for AI and data centers (following the US midterms)," Ryu said at the event. "It (actually) provides a golden opportunity to narrow our gap with leading countries and secure overwhelming national AI competitiveness through aggressive and speedy investments and technological innovation," he added.

results.title: Memorial wall set up for fallen elite Ethiopian troops fighting in Korean War
results.content: A memorial wall has been set up in Ethiopia to honor fallen members of an elite Ethiopian unit that won all of the 253 battles it engaged in during the 1950-53 Korean War, Seoul's veterans ministry said Wednesday. An unveiling ceremony was held Wednesday (local time) at a cathedral in Addis Ababa for the memorial wall displaying the names of 122 Ethiopian troops who served under the Kagnew Battalion and died during the war, according to the ministry. Ethiopia is the only African nation that deployed ground troops to fight for South Korea during the three-year conflict. The Kagnew Battalion, an elite force comprising some 3,500 Ethiopian Royal Guards, won all 253 battles it engaged in, with some 122 of the soldiers losing their lives in the process. results.title: NK fishermen rescued off Ulleung Island seek to defect, testing Lee administration
results.content: Some of the North Korean fishermen rescued off Ulleung Island reportedly want to defect, posing a test for President Lee Jae Myung’s administration as it seeks dialogue with Pyongyang. They were among the six fishermen aboard a boat that the Navy and Coast Guard found drifting in international waters north of the island on Nov. 3. Others reportedly wish to return to North Korea, with authorities questioning each crew member to establish their final wishes. They could become the first North Koreans to defect following a publicly reported rescue since Lee took office in June 2025, at a time when his government appears to favor a low-key approach to avoid provoking Pyongyang and resume talks. results.title: NC swings to profit, Nexon beats expectations as Krafton struggles
results.content: Korean game developers have reported mixed third-quarter earnings. NC returned to profitability from a year earlier, while Nexon defied market pessimism with solid revenue from its live service games. Krafton, meanwhile, saw its operating profit decline as revenue from PUBG: Battlegrounds (PUBG) failed to keep pace with rising costs associated with its business diversification efforts. NC announced its third-quarter earnings Wednesday, reporting sales of 686.5 billion won ($514.2 million) and an operating profit of 119.6 billion won. Revenue surged 91 percent year-on-year, while the company swung to an operating profit from a loss of 750 million won in the same period last year. Overseas sales accounted for 54 percent of total revenue, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of growth in their share, as the company continued to expand its global revenue base, particularly in North America

results.title: LG Innotek earns top cooperation rating for 10th consecutive year
results.content: LG Innotek said Wednesday it received the highest rating in the 2025 Win-Win Growth Index assessment conducted by the Korea Commission for Corporate Partnership, marking its 10th consecutive year at the top level. The index evaluates companies' efforts to promote mutually beneficial partnerships with suppliers and classifies them into five grades, ranging from outstanding to very inadequate. LG Innotek has maintained the highest possible rating since the 2016 assessment, reflecting its sustained efforts to strengthen partnerships with suppliers. Recognizing that suppliers' competitiveness directly contributes to its own, the company has steadily expanded its support programs to address changing business conditions. results.title: Korea, Indonesia discuss diversifying defense industry cooperation
results.content: Korea and Indonesia on Wednesday discussed efforts to diversify their defense industry cooperation, including co-development of defense assets and joint arms exports to third markets, Seoul's arms agency said. The topics were addressed during a regular bilateral meeting on defense industry cooperation in Jakarta, led by officials from the Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) and Indonesia's defense ministry, DAPA said. "Officials discussed ways to diversify partnership models between the two countries' defense firms, including joint development, local production and joint exports to third-party markets," the arms agency said. Both sides also reviewed the status of major ongoing defense cooperation projects and discussed follow-up steps to implement them, it added. results.title: Crimes that bespeak anger, isolation
results.content: With the nation’s top police office left vacant for nearly the past two years, a self-identified worrywart like me is left pondering whether an organization with structural layers of dedicated police officers can keep functioning. Finally, though, President Lee Jae Myung has named his pick for the next commissioner general of the Korean National Police Agency (KNPA). He nominated incumbent Deputy Commissioner General Kim Jong-chul, in what can be seen as a safe promotion. Vital to our security, police assume an ever-greater presence amid the Lee administration’s agenda of reforming the prosecution and law enforcement. results.title: [COVER STORY] AI glasses solve 4 CSAT math questions in 10 seconds
results.content: At an optical store in Seoul’s Myeong-dong shopping area, I looked through a pair of Rokid artificial intelligence (AI) glasses at a page of four math questions from a mock version of the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT). Within 10 seconds, answers and explanations appeared inside the lenses, before I had even finished making sense of the first question. All four were correct. I then tested the glasses with another math question — this time a calculus problem involving a definite integral. The correct answer appeared in under two seconds. “This is the very product that has been in the controversy lately over cheating,” the optician said. It was a brief demonstration, not a controlled accuracy test. results.title: Homeplus faces deepening survival crisis; union calls for government aid
results.content: Homeplus, which is undergoing court-led corporate rehabilitation, is facing a deepening survival crisis amid mounting financial difficulties, including unpaid supplier bills, delayed wages and overdue utility payments, industry officials said Wednesday. The company's prolonged search for a buyer has added to uncertainty over its future, prompting its labor union to urge the government to provide emergency funding to prevent further job losses. The major supermarket chain filed for rehabilitation with the Seoul Bankruptcy Court in March last year following a credit rating downgrade. It subsequently suspended operations at some stores before reopening some of them in mid-August this year, but continues to struggle with weak sales and supply disruptions. results.title: Korea sets sights on runway-free aircraft after record-breaking drone flight
results.content: Korea is pushing ahead with plans for a new generation of aircraft that can take off and land without runways, following a record-setting seven-day flight by its solar-powered unmanned aircraft in the stratosphere. The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA) announced Wednesday that it will pursue development of hybrid vertical takeoff and landing aircraft after its EAV-4 unmanned aerial vehicle completed 170 hours and 5 minutes of continuous flight from Aug. 18 to 25. The achievement more than tripled Korea's previous domestic endurance record of 53 hours, set by the EAV-3 in 2020, and ranked second globally behind Airbus' Zephyr, according to the agency. results.title: Hana Financial kicks off annual volunteering campaign with kimchi-making event
results.content: Hana Financial Group launched its annual two-month volunteer campaign, kicking it off with a kimchi-making event for vulnerable households, the company said Wednesday. The group held a launch ceremony for its "Everyone's Hana Day" campaign at its Seoul office, followed by a kimchi-making event attended by about 250 people, including Chairman Ham Young-joo, employees and their families. At Wednesday's event, participants prepared 11,111 heads of kimchi for distribution to people in need. Ham and other employees also visited a welfare facility for people with disabilities in Yongsan District, Seoul, to deliver kimchi and daily necessities. results.title: HD Construction Equipment, veterans ministry unveil Korean War memorial in Ethiopia
results.content: HD Construction Equipment has joined hands with the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to honor Ethiopian soldiers who fought and died during the 1950-53 Korean War, unveiling a memorial wall bearing their names at Holy Trinity Cathedral in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The company said it held a ceremony to dedicate the memorial wall at the cathedral on Wednesday, coinciding with the International Memorial Day for U.N. Korean War Veterans. The event was attended by HD Construction Equipment CEO Moon Jae-young, Veterans Minister Kwon Oh-eul, Korean Ambassador to Ethiopia Koo Hong-seok, Ethiopian defense officials and Korean War veterans and their families. HD Construction Equipment and the veterans ministry signed a memorandum of understanding in May to establish memorial facilities in countries that sent troops to support Korea under U.N. Command.
